about: A notebook for longer, more abstract writing than a diary entry. An entry is a fact about a day ("went to the pool with @A"); a notebook document is a thought worked through in prose, and it is expected to change over months. Documents live in a tree — a document can contain other documents, and the containing one is still fully writable, so there is no separate "folder" concept to name. Every day a document changes is kept, and the plugin can show what changed between any two of those days. These strings are fetched only once the user enables the plugin, and are merged into the app's main bundle under the `plugins.notebook.` prefix — a key written here as "title" is referenced in code as plugins.notebook.title.

notebook.where: The plugin's own page at /plugins/notebook, which is one page shape reused at every level (a document's prose, with the documents inside it listed beneath, and a breadcrumb back to the top); a card on the diary's day page below the composer, shown on today always and on a past day only if something was written that day; its name and description in the Plugins list in Settings; a settings card of its own beneath that switch, for the one device-local image-caching option; the Calendar page's month grid once its name appears as a tab, shaded green by how much was written each day; the plugin's own export type in Settings → Markdown export, alongside Entries and People; and a three-screen tour opened from beside its switch in Settings.

keys.name: The plugin's name in the Plugins list in Settings. A noun phrase. Choose a word for a bound book of one's own writing — not "notes", which in this app already means the free-text field on a person's profile, and not a word implying something fleeting or disposable.
keys.description: One line under the name in the Plugins list, explaining what enabling it does.
keys.title: Heading of the plugin's own page and its day card, the first breadcrumb (i.e. the top of the tree), the calendar tab, and the Markdown export's heading. Usually identical to `name`.
keys.untitled: Stands in for a document with no title *and* no text to take a first line from. A title is optional by design — the first line of the body is used when there isn't one — so this appears only for a document that is genuinely still empty.
keys.new: Button creating a new document inside whichever one is open. One word; on a narrow screen only its icon shows.
keys.open: Button on the day card that goes to the plugin's own page. One word.
keys.inside: Small heading above the list of documents contained by the one being viewed. A preposition or short phrase meaning "contained by this one" — not "children" or "sub-documents", which name a data structure rather than what the reader sees.
keys.noChildren: Shown in place of that list when the open document contains nothing yet. Matter-of-fact, not an instruction.
keys.breadcrumb: Accessible name of the breadcrumb navigation. Never visible.
keys.documentActions: Accessible name of the ⋯ button holding focus mode, history, move and delete. Never visible.
keys.emptyTitle: Shown on the plugin's own page when the whole notebook is empty.
keys.emptyDescription: Second line of that empty state. Says what a document is for (more than a bullet point — the diary already has bullet points) and that documents nest.
keys.titleLabel: Accessible name of the title input, which appears in place of the page heading once it is clicked. There is no visible label — the heading *is* the field.
keys.titlePlaceholder: Placeholder in that input, shown while a document has no title of its own. Usually the same word as `untitled`.
keys.titleEditHint: Hover tooltip on the page heading, which is editable in place: a dotted underline is the only other hint. An action in the imperative — "Click to rename" — not a description of the state.
keys.bodyPlaceholder: Placeholder in the empty document body. Mentions the things that are not obvious: Markdown is understood, typing @ offers a list of people, and typing [[ offers a list of documents to link to. Keep it inviting rather than instructional.
keys.mentionSuggestions: Accessible name of the list of people that appears while typing @. Never visible.
keys.documentMentionSuggestions: Accessible name of the list of documents that appears while typing [[, the counterpart of `mentionSuggestions` for linking to another document instead of a person. Never visible.
keys.edit: Button label returning from the rendered preview to the Markdown source. On a narrow screen only its icon shows.
keys.preview: The same button's label while editing, offering the rendered view.
keys.previewEmpty: Shown in the preview pane when the document has no text yet.
keys.taskCheckbox: Fallback accessible name for a `- [ ]` task item's checkbox in the preview, used only when the item's own text is empty (an unwritten task line). Ordinarily the checkbox is named by the task's own text instead, so this is rarely what a screen reader actually announces. A short, generic noun — "Task" or equivalent.
keys.imageNotFound: Shown in place of a `![alt](url)` image that failed to load — no network, a dead link, or offline with nothing cached. Also doubles as that placeholder's accessible name when the image itself had no alt text. Plain and factual, not an apology.
keys.tooLong: Shown when a document has grown past the size a row can hold. The *only* status this screen ever shows — there is deliberately no "saving" indicator, because a write reaches the local database immediately and syncing is the sync pill's business. So this line has to be clear that nothing is being saved right now and that shortening the document fixes it: it is the one state in the plugin where writing is genuinely not being kept. {{over}} is a number of bytes.
keys.focus: Menu item hiding everything except the text, for writing on a small screen. A short noun phrase.
keys.history: Menu item opening the day-by-day history of the open document.
keys.historyTitle: Title of that dialog. The document's own name is shown beneath it, so this does not need to repeat it.
keys.historyEmpty: Shown in that dialog for a document created but never written in.
keys.charactersAdded: The calendar cell's tooltip: how much the notebook *grew* on that day — what was written less what was cut, never below zero. Digits and a unit; it sits in a tooltip and nothing else. Note this is a narrower question than the day card asks with `charactersDeltaLabel`: a day spent rewriting shows here as a quiet one, on purpose, because the grid is about what is there now that was not there before.
keys.noNetGrowth: Shown in the same place for a day whose recorded figure is zero — an edit typed and undone, leaving the document exactly as it was found. Must not read as "nothing happened": someone sat down with it.
keys.diffBetween: Header above the comparison, naming its two ends. Both {{from}} and {{to}} arrive as already-formatted dates. An arrow between two dates is fine; no extra words are needed.
keys.diffFirstDay: The same header for the earliest day on record, which has no previous day to compare against — so what is shown is the document appearing from nothing. {{date}} is already formatted.
keys.diffNoChange: Shown when the two chosen days turn out identical.
keys.move: Menu item opening the destination picker. Ends in an ellipsis, as an action that opens a dialog rather than doing something immediately.
keys.moveDescription: Under the title. {{name}} is the document being moved; use the quotation marks of the target language. Must say that the contents move with it.
keys.moveConfirm: The dialog's confirming button. One word.
keys.delete: Menu item deleting the open document.
keys.deleteDescription: Body of that dialog. {{name}} is the document; use the target language's quotation marks. Must say two things: the contents go too, and the history goes too. Deliberately does *not* claim the delete is permanent — the toast that follows carries an Undo, the same as every other delete in this app.
keys.deleted: Toast after a successful delete. The count includes the documents that were inside the one deleted, which is why it is a count rather than a name.
keys.dayPrompt: The one line the day card shows on a day nothing has been written. An open question, asked once and never repeated — there is no notification behind it and no streak to keep. It should read as an invitation, never as a reminder or a nudge.
keys.touchedToday: Small caption above the list of documents written in today, on the day card. Deliberately not a count in English (the list is right underneath); a language whose grammar needs the number may use {{count}}.
keys.touchedThatDay: The same caption on a past day's card, in the past tense.
keys.charactersDeltaLabel: The accessible name for the two figures at the end of each row on the day card, which read visually as "+120 −45". The digits and the signs are drawn directly and are not translated; this is the sentence a screen reader gets instead, because two bare numbers and a symbol are not one. Both counts are real: characters written that day and characters taken out, never a single net figure — a day spent cutting a thought down is work, and a net number reports it as nothing.
keys.exportHint: Small note under the output-mode picker in Settings → Markdown export, once this plugin's own export type is chosen there. That dialog is generic and shows this plugin's `name` as the option's label and this string underneath the picker — it never names the plugin itself, so this is the one place that gets to say, in the plugin's own voice, what the export actually contains (a frontmatter block per document) and what it leaves out (history).
keys.settingsTitle: Heading of the plugin's settings card in Settings, beneath its on/off switch. Names what the card is about — this card holds exactly one setting, image caching, so name that rather than repeating the plugin's own name.
keys.settingsDescription: One line under that heading, explaining what the setting below does and why it might matter: images linked from a document can be kept on this device so they still show with no connection.
keys.cacheImages: Label of the one switch on that card. A short, direct phrase — "Cache images" or equivalent — not a full sentence.
keys.cacheImagesDescription: Explanation under that switch. Must say what it costs (this device's storage) as plainly as what it buys (images keep working offline), the same even-handedness `settingsDescription` above and the app's own `syncOnWifiOnly` setting both use for a similar trade-off. Off by default; this text does not need to say so, `settingsDescription` already sets the context.
keys.onboarding.tree.title: Heading of the tour's first screen, whose single idea is that there is no separate folder type. Reachable from a button beside the plugin's switch in Settings, not from the app's first-run tour.
keys.onboarding.tree.lede: One line under that heading, saying that a containing document can itself be written in — which is what makes a group able to explain itself.
keys.onboarding.tree.crumb: In the mocked-up screenshot: the parent shown in the breadcrumb, one level above the document being viewed. A broad, ordinary area of interest — pick what sounds natural in the target language rather than translating literally.
keys.onboarding.tree.heading: In the same mock-up: the title of the document being viewed. A subject broad enough to plausibly contain the three documents listed under it, since that is the whole point being made.
keys.onboarding.tree.body: In the same mock-up: a couple of lines of that document's own prose, cut off mid-thought with an ellipsis. It must read as real, unfinished thinking rather than an encyclopedia entry — this is both the tone the plugin is for and the evidence for the screen's claim, which is that the document holding others is itself something you write in.
keys.onboarding.tree.childOne: First of three documents listed inside it in the mock-up. These are areas *within* the parent subject, not fragments of the sentence above them.
keys.onboarding.tree.childThree: Third of the three. Deliberately the longest, so the mock-up shows how a long title is truncated in the list.
keys.onboarding.history.title: Heading of the tour's second screen: a real diff, rendered by the app's own diff code, between two versions of an example thought.
keys.onboarding.history.lede: One line under it, naming what the history is *for* — seeing how a thought moved, not just where it ended.
keys.onboarding.history.caption: Small caption above the diff, naming the day being shown. A date written out in the target language's usual style.
keys.onboarding.history.before: Two short notes in one document, as they stood the day before. Contains a literal newline escape (\n\n) separating them, which must be preserved: the diff is computed line by line, and the screen shows nothing useful if each version is a single line.
keys.onboarding.history.after: The same two notes the next day. Keep the two-paragraph shape and the \n\n, and keep both *kinds* of change, since they are what the red and green lines demonstrate: the first line is refined (the same claim, narrowed by a condition), and the second is reversed outright (something once intended to be tried, since found to make no difference). Together they show the two things a history is for — watching a thought get sharper, and watching one turn out to be wrong.
keys.onboarding.calendar.title: Heading of the tour's third screen: three weeks of the calendar's Notebook tab, drawn with the app's real tab switcher, weekday headings and less-to-more legend, shaded by the app's own function in the plugin's registered green.
keys.onboarding.calendar.lede: One line under it, carrying two facts: darker means more written that day across the whole notebook, and a day spent cutting rather than adding shows as a quiet one — a deliberate choice, so word it matter-of-factly rather than apologetically.

tone: Same as the main app: plain, calm, second person, no exclamation marks. Closer to reflective than to productive — this plugin is for thinking, so nothing should sound like a task manager, and nothing should imply an obligation to write. Never congratulate the user for writing and never chide them for not.

languageNotes.en: Reference language; source strings are authored here.
languageNotes.es: Tú, not usted, matching the rest of the app.
languageNotes.it: Tu, not Lei, matching the rest of the app.
languageNotes.ja: です・ます, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `charactersAdded`, `deleted`, `touchedToday` and `touchedThatDay` keys are needed — Japanese has a single plural category.
languageNotes.zh: Simplified Chinese, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed forms of the same four keys are needed — Chinese has a single plural category.
